name: Underinsurance turns loss into household debt and stalled rebuilds
pillar_note: Moderates DL -> SL: share underinsured/uninsured changes how much DL becomes household loss; also feeds FP when governments fill the gap
description: Low sums insured, debris costs inside the sum insured and rising rebuild costs -> payouts fall short -> owners take bigger mortgages, rely on charity, or never rebuild
affected_group: Homeowners and small businesses in fire-prone areas
key_quant_evidence: Black Saturday: ~30% of 2,029 destroyed homes underinsured, ~13% possibly uninsured (Royal Commission); >65% of Blue Mountains 2013 households underinsured (ABC); Marshall Fire 74% underinsured (CU Boulder)
exp7_result: Not tested. Experiment 7 only noted insurance (A$2.3bn) as one reason local income looked normal; underinsurance rates were never measured.
best_data: ICA Historical Normalised Catastrophe list (claims and incurred) (event / state, per event, open); ATO Taxation Statistics individuals by postcode (Table 8 median and average taxable income) (postcode, annual, open)
record_ids: lit-22 lit-23 gov-55 news-23 news-25 survey-6 survey-8 survey-10 news-51 news-52 news-28 news-58

name: Peak-season tourism shutdown in fire regions
pillar_note: IL: regional visitor spend / accommodation takings by quarter; tourism jobs at workplaces in fire councils
description: Fires and evacuation orders over Christmas-January -> visitors cancel or are ordered out -> tourism and hospitality turnover collapses in the fire region; peak-season income is not made up later, partial rebound when visitors return
affected_group: Regional tourism and hospitality businesses and workers
key_quant_evidence: South Coast NSW visitor spend -23% (A$251m) in Mar qtr 2020 (TRA); A$2.8b output and about 7,300 jobs lost nationally (Reiner et al.); about half of 120 Merimbula chamber members had takings down 60%+ (Region)
exp7_result: SA2 accommodation and food-services income per 10pp homes-inside-fire, years 0-2: +6.0% [-0.4,+12.4], not detected (opposite of expected, Day 10). Visitor spend, nights and the Dec-Jan quarter were NOT tested; annual income would hide a peak-season shock partly caught up later.
best_data: Local Government Area and Tourism Region profiles (visitor nights, spend, day trips) (Tourism region (quarterly); LGA profiles (annual, pooled), quarterly for regions; annual for LGA, open); Jobs in Australia, Accommodation and Food Services employee jobs (SA2 by industry, annual, open); Spendmapp card-spending data (LGA, some postcode; by category (accommodation, dining), daily/monthly, paid)
record_ids: lit-1 gov-14 gov-40 gov-43 news-19 news-64 news-61 survey-15 survey-20 survey-21

name: Fire exposure -> long-lasting mental ill-health
pillar_note: SL: mental-health service use (MBS mental-health items, GP visits) per 1,000 in fire areas
description: Life threat, loss and evacuation -> PTSD, depression and anxiety that stay high for years, reducing capacity to work and adding health costs
affected_group: Directly exposed adults and young people
key_quant_evidence: About 1 in 5 high-exposure people at PTSD cut-off 12-18 months on, n=3,083 (ANU survey); PTSD 21% at 5 years in high-impact Black Saturday communities (Beyond Bushfires); ~62.6% felt recovered at 10 years
exp7_result: Not tested; no health indicator has been used in Experiment 7.
best_data: Medicare-subsidised mental health-specific services (persons and services by type) (SA3, PHN, state, remoteness, annual (financial year), open); Medicare-subsidised GP, allied health and specialist care across local areas (SA3, PHN, annual, open); HealthStats NSW: mental health related emergency department visits (monthly) (NSW and Local Health District pages, monthly, open)
record_ids: lit-13 gov-22 survey-1 survey-3 lit-52 gov-12 gov-2 survey-42 survey-43

name: Recovery grants slow, opaque and politically allocated
pillar_note: FP: grant timing and allocation by council (BLER/BCRRF per capita vs DL)
description: Reimbursement-style grants, delays and minimum thresholds set by ministers -> money arrives late and goes to some electorates over others; charities also hold back funds
key_quant_evidence: BLER A$541.8m with A$1m minimum threshold (Audit Office NSW); 26 first-round grants to Coalition seats, 0 to Blue Mountains (Inside Local Government); ~48% of A$2.74b delivered by end 2020 (SBS)
exp7_result: Experiment 7 Day 10 DETECTED council grants +A$330 per resident per 10 homes destroyed per 1,000 [+65,+742] in the year after fire (OLG time series). Black Summer programs reported A$677m vs 2,480 homes (~A$270k/home). Day 11: all grants +A$56/resident [-295,+386] over a 3-year view, diluted one-off spike. NOT tested: timing within the year (months), which electorates/councils got first-round grants vs losses, delay to payment.
best_data: OLG Time-Series Data (Your Council), council financial data returns (LGA (council), annual (financial year), open); Bushfire recovery programs evaluation reports (summary, BLER Stage 1, BLER Stage 2 & BIRP Stream 2, BIRP Stream 1, BCRRF Phase 1) on the NSW Government bushfire recovery page (project and LGA level (inside PDFs and an interactive map; no CSV list seen on the page), project-level dates (approval/completion), would need hand-extraction, open); Performance audit report: Bushfire recovery grants (Audit Office of NSW) (program-level; any council tables are inside the PDF (unverified), program dates (A$1m minimum threshold, delays), open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: The '~48% of A$2.74b delivered' figure (news-55) comes from an advocacy-commissioned report, and news-56 shows the government disputed it (A$1.9b claimed). Present both. The political-allocation claim is well supported by the Audit Office (gov-30).
record_ids: gov-30 gov-31 survey-63 news-55 news-56 gov-27 news-29 gov-57

name: Housing stock loss -> rents up and overcrowding
pillar_note: SL: median rent change and rental affordability (bond lodgements by postcode); overcrowding
description: Destroyed homes shrink supply while displaced households compete for rentals (plus holiday-let share) -> rents rise, overcrowding and homelessness risk grow, worst for low-income renters
key_quant_evidence: Rent +A$20/week (~10%), +A$26 (13%) in disadvantaged areas after Black Summer (Akter & Grafton); Camp Fire: nearby prices +13% within six weeks (Hennighausen & James); Eurobodalla rents up almost 50% in five years to Dec 2022 (Region)
exp7_result: Council-level new-bond rents, year after: +0.1% per 10 homes destroyed per 1,000 [-1.6,+1.2], not detected. The +10% rent finding in the literature was at very small areas 2016-2021 and overlaps the covid regional rent boom. Postcode-month level, bond counts (supply) and Census overcrowding have NOT been tested.
best_data: Rental bond data: monthly lodgements (dwelling type, weekly rent, bedrooms), quarterly refunds, annual holdings (postcode, monthly (lodgements), quarterly (refunds), annual (holdings), open); Census DataPacks GCP: rent paid, dwelling structure, bedrooms/household size (overcrowding) (SA1, SA2, POA, Census 5-yearly, open); DSS Commonwealth Rent Assistance recipients by Income Unit type (postcode, LGA, SA2, quarterly, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: The rent figures (+A$20/10%, +A$26/13%) are confirmed in news-33, but they come from the same 2016-2021 Census design that overlaps the COVID regional rent boom. Experiment 7 found no detectable council-level rent effect. 'Strong' should be 'moderate', with the confound stated.
record_ids: lit-4 lit-14 lit-44 news-2 news-34 survey-31 survey-56 survey-69 gov-32

name: Slow rebuilding -> long-term displacement
pillar_note: SL: share of destroyed homes rebuilt after N years (building approvals / completions in fire areas)
description: Bushfire building standards, approvals, material inflation and builder shortages raise cost and delay rebuilds -> families live in caravans, sheds or pods for years; case support ends before they are rehoused
affected_group: Homeowners who lost houses, older and lower-income people
key_quant_evidence: Bega Valley: ~50 of 464 destroyed homes rebuilt after five years (SBS); BAL compliance can add up to ~A$100,000 (NSW Inquiry via Mondaq); rebuilds can take 3-4 years (IDMC)
exp7_result: Not tested. Construction sector counts after fires were checked (-1.0% per 10pp [-3.4,+1.4], not detected) but that is not a rebuilding rate. Day 8 predicted homes destroyed, not rebuilt.
best_data: Building Approvals by SA2 and above (dwelling units, value; monthly CSV by SA2) (SA2 (also SA3, SA4, GCCSA, LGA cubes), monthly, open); Census 2016 vs 2021 dwelling counts by SA1/SA2 (GCP) (SA1, SA2, Census 5-yearly, open); Rebuild completion or DA/CDC approval lists for bushfire-destroyed homes (address/lot, event dates, request/restricted)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: Checked SBS (news-1). 'About 50 of 464 Bega Valley homes rebuilt' is a claim by an advocacy group founder (Social Justice Advocates of the Sapphire Coast), not an official count. Label it as an advocate estimate. The 'strong' rating rests mostly on first-person accounts.
record_ids: news-1 gov-33 lit-49 survey-61 news-21 news-27 news-60 gov-61 news-22

name: Domestic and family violence rises
pillar_note: SL: DV incidents per 1,000 (BOCSAR, monthly by LGA)
description: Stress, financial and housing loss, alcohol, and stretched or cut-off services -> more domestic violence, including from previously non-violent partners; evacuation centres expose women to former partners
key_quant_evidence: Women in worst-affected Black Saturday areas reported IPV ~7 times the rate of less-affected (Flinders review); 16 of 30 women reported violence since the fires, 9 new (Parkinson, AJEM)
exp7_result: Not tested; no crime or safety outcome used in Experiment 7.
best_data: Quarterly recorded crime dataset by Suburb (62 offences incl. domestic violence related assault; monthly counts) (suburb (also postcode and LGA), monthly counts (published quarterly), open); Quarterly recorded crime dataset by LGA (RCI_offencebymonth.xlsm) (LGA, monthly, open); NSW Crime Tool (maps and summaries by LGA, suburb, postcode) (LGA, suburb, postcode, annual/quarterly summaries, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: lit-20 (PreventionWeb) returned 403 so the '~7 times' figure could not be verified. It comes from Black Saturday (Victoria) research, not NSW Black Summer. news-48, news-49 and survey-46 are warnings, not measurements, and survey-58 is anecdotal. Evidence for Black Summer NSW should be 'moderate', and the table should say no measured NSW Black Summer increase was found.
record_ids: lit-20 gov-35 gov-48 news-48 news-49 survey-44 survey-45 survey-46

name: Public payments and charity cushion the loss
pillar_note: Moderator on SL; also FP spending: disaster payments per capita by LGA
description: Flat disaster payments, income allowances, back-to-school grants, replanting funds and charity cash -> fast relief that offsets part of income loss, but at fixed rates not matched to need
key_quant_evidence: Over A$283m paid by July 2020 (A$1,000/adult, A$400/child) (Services Australia); Red Cross over A$119m to 4,380 people (IDMC); 200,000+ individual payments (SBS)
exp7_result: Council grants per resident rose A$330 per 10 homes destroyed per 1,000 [+65, +742], detected (Day 10 A). Gross cost, grants received and net cost borne by councils were not detected in the 3-year window (Day 11: net +A$58 per resident [-377, +451]). Individual payments (DRP, income support) not tested separately; SA2 DSS welfare not detected.
best_data: Location-Based Disaster Assistance Payments (AGDRP, DRA, DRFA measures by LGA) (LGA (suburb-level data summed to LGA, so may double count), per disaster event (monthly of payment not seen), open); DRFA Activation History by LGA (LGA, per event, open); NSW bushfire grants, payments and financial support (programs list and LGA examples) (program and LGA text, event, open)
critic_note: Critic: disaster payments are public spending (FP); cushioning SL is a secondary moderator role.
record_ids: gov-51 gov-36 survey-62 survey-65 survey-7 gov-45 survey-33 gov-42 gov-44

name: Smoke health burden and health-system cost
pillar_note: SL: respiratory ED visits/admissions per 1,000; FP: public health spending
description: Smoke -> deaths, hospital admissions, ED visits and symptoms well beyond burnt areas -> health-system and household costs
affected_group: People with heart/lung conditions, smoke-affected cities
key_quant_evidence: 417 excess deaths, 3,151 hospitalisations, ~A$1.95b health cost, NSW A$1.07b (Borchers Arriagada et al., MJA); NSW respiratory ED visits up to 50% higher in some areas (AIHW)
exp7_result: Not tested; no air-quality or health outcome in Experiment 7.
best_data: NSW Air Quality monitoring network data download and Data Explorer (PM2.5, PM10, ozone) (monitoring station (point), hourly (aggregate to daily/monthly), open); HealthStats NSW: asthma and unplanned ED presentations (monthly) (NSW and Local Health District, monthly, open); AIHW Medicare-subsidised GP, allied health, specialist use across local areas (SA3, PHN, annual, open)
critic_note: Critic: smoke exposure itself should enter as an X variable (smoke days per council-fire), not a separate smoke study.
record_ids: lit-21 gov-11 gov-13 lit-40 news-50 survey-26 survey-28

name: Small business closure (cash-flow failure, anchor facility lost)
pillar_note: IL: business counts / closures (ABS CABEE) in fire councils
description: Lost peak trade plus thin cash buffers and weak business-interruption cover -> small firms close or depend on aid; loss of an anchor facility takes seasonal jobs from nearby towns
affected_group: Small and young businesses and their staff
key_quant_evidence: 17% of SMEs closed temporarily, 24% in vulnerable areas (NAB); small business 65-72% of economic impact, only 44% had BI cover in Townsville (IAG/SGS); Selwyn resort shut 3+ years, ~100 seasonal jobs (ABC)
exp7_result: ABS CABEE business counts by SA2: sum over two June years +0.1% [-1.3,+1.6] vs similar areas; business numbers falling more than about 13% over two years were ruled out (about 6.6% a year if persistent) (Day 7). Not tested: closures of specific anchor facilities, or small and young businesses separately.
best_data: Counts of Australian Businesses incl. Entries and Exits (CABEE) (SA2 (cubes), LGA, industry, employment size, annual (June), open); ASIC insolvency statistics (state / industry; no postcode in public tables, monthly/quarterly, open); Government disaster-grant lists for small business (Service NSW / NSW Reconstruction Authority / Disaster Assist) (LGA (counts); postcode if requested, per disaster, request/restricted)
record_ids: news-4 survey-13 survey-17 lit-36 news-54 gov-60

name: Rebuilding and health sectors gain (sectoral winners)
pillar_note: IL: net vs gross indirect loss; construction jobs as an offset term in IL
description: Rebuilding spending, insurance payouts and health demand -> construction, real-estate and health workers earn more, partly offsetting losses; this can hide losses in aggregate GRP
key_quant_evidence: Healthcare workers +8% income (Ulubasoglu & Beaini); after Qld floods low earners -A$3,100, middle/high +A$3,770/+A$3,380 (Ulubasoglu 2020); US hurricane earnings negative year 1, positive from year 3 (Groen et al.)
exp7_result: SA2 construction-sector income per 10pp homes-inside-fire, years 0-2: -1.0% [-3.4,+1.4], not detected; the expected rise was not seen (Day 10). Council grants per resident rose +A$330 per 10 homes/1,000 (detected, but that is FP not IL). Monthly building approvals and rebuild employment were NOT tested.
best_data: Building Approvals, Australia (SA2 data cubes) (SA2 (and LGA), monthly, open); NSW Planning Portal development application open data (address / LGA, daily lodgement and determination dates, free registration); Jobs in Australia, Construction and Health employee jobs (SA2 by industry, annual, open)
record_ids: lit-9 survey-37 lit-18 lit-37 gov-16 lit-47 survey-39

name: Premiums and insurance taxes push people out of cover
pillar_note: X / Moderator: pre-fire insurance affordability (premium-to-income) as an exposure condition; post-fire premium rise as an SL cost
description: Address-level risk pricing, levies and stamp duty raise premiums -> households cut or drop cover before a fire; after a fire, perceived risk pushes premiums up further; mitigation could lower them
affected_group: Households and small businesses in high-risk areas
key_quant_evidence: Emergency Services Levy and taxes over 50% of NSW premiums (ICA via Insurance News, industry claim); monthly-payment surcharges up to 20% (ACCC)
exp7_result: Not tested. No fire-matched premium or take-up data have been used.
best_data: Property Insurance Affordability (illustrative postcode premium mapping) (postcode (maps in paper), snapshot, request/restricted); Climate Risk Map (Climate Valuation modelled risk and 'uninsurable by 2030' share) (federal electorate in report; address-level in the proprietary map, snapshot, projected to 2030, paid); ATO Taxation Statistics by postcode (income, for premium-to-income ratio) (postcode, annual, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: 'ESL and taxes over 50% of NSW premiums' is an Insurance Council claim relayed by survey-9, and the record itself notes a conflicting 70% figure. It is an industry advocacy number and should not stand as evidence without a primary source.
record_ids: gov-10 gov-20 gov-21 survey-9 news-53 gov-17 gov-62

name: Who benefits from aid (targeting and regressivity)
pillar_note: FP: share of recovery spending reaching households vs businesses vs infrastructure
description: Recovery money goes mainly to business, infrastructure and main-street projects, and to people with assets and borrowing power -> households, renters and farmers get less, so aid can widen gaps
key_quant_evidence: Qld floods: ~10% of recovery spending to income help, ~80% to businesses (Ulubasoglu); ~20% of recovery grants to farm/food businesses (WWF); Harvey SBA/FEMA aid regressive (Billings et al.)
exp7_result: Experiment 7 Day 10 showed grants to councils rose with homes lost (DETECTED) and Day 5/6/7 found households' income, unemployment, welfare per 1,000 not detectably changed (income support rise < +4.5/1,000, council income fall < 1.6%). Day 9 found SA2 total income -1.6% per 10pp (DETECTED, fewer earners). The split of recovery money between households, businesses and infrastructure was NOT measured.
best_data: Location-Based Disaster Assistance Payments (AGDRP, Disaster Recovery Allowance, DRFA measures by LGA) (LGA, per disaster event (annual/event totals), open); Disaster Recovery Payment and Disaster Recovery Allowance Management Information (activation / event level, event, open); DSS Payment Demographic Data (quarterly) (SA2, postcode, LGA, electorate (SA2 from 2015), quarterly, open)
record_ids: lit-12 lit-29 lit-15 news-36 news-3 gov-59

name: Power, telecom and road outages stop trade
pillar_note: IL: outage-days per council as a short-run IL driver; X: dependence on single power/road link
description: Mains power loss (not fire damage) knocks out phone towers, EFTPOS and bookings, and roads close -> towns cannot trade or sell fuel and food for days; stock spoils
affected_group: Businesses and residents in cut-off towns
key_quant_evidence: 888 outages of 4+ hours, 88% from power loss and 1% from fire damage, average 3.5 days, 1,406 facilities (ACMA); 818 Telstra facilities hit in NSW
exp7_result: Power, telecom or road outages were not tested in Experiment 7.
best_data: Impact of 2019-20 bushfires on telecommunications networks (outage report and facility lists) (facility / LGA in report tables, event (Aug 2019-Feb 2020), open); Transport for NSW open data / Live Traffic incident feed (road segment, minutes (current feed), free registration); NSW RFS major incidents / evacuation notices (incident, live, open)

name: Who pays / opportunity cost of recovery spending
pillar_note: FP: recovery spend per capita vs mitigation spend; council maintenance burden of rebuilt assets
description: Large recovery budgets (shared Commonwealth/NSW) -> money spent rebuilding is not spent on mitigation or other services; facilities rebuilt for a shrunken town later force rate rises
key_quant_evidence: Commonwealth mitigation spend ~3% of post-disaster spend (Productivity Commission 2014); A$4.4bn NSW recovery programs, NSW share A$3bn (Regional NSW); Marysville A$1.72m/yr maintenance, 18% rate rise proposed (ABC)
exp7_result: Not tested. Experiment 7 measured how much money came in (Day 10, Day 11) but not recovery spending versus mitigation spending, or the later maintenance burden of rebuilt assets.
best_data: Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements (DRFA) cash estimates by state, Budget Paper No. 3 (State (NSW), annual forward estimates, open); OLG Time-Series Data: asset renewal, infrastructure backlog, operating result, rates and grants (LGA, annual, open); DRFA Activation History by LGA (LGA, per event (activation date), open)

name: Council budget gap (lost revenue plus extra spending)
pillar_note: FP: council own-source revenue gap and operating result (NSW OLG data) after fires
description: Fires raise council spending and cut rates and fee income (rate relief only partly reimbursed) -> net deficit and crowd-out of roads and services, worst for small rural councils
key_quant_evidence: California: deficit probability +25 pp, excess revenue -US$97/person (Liao & Kousky); Lockyer Valley A$42.5m = 88% of annual revenue (PC submission); Eurobodalla rate reimbursement ~A$300,000 short
exp7_result: Experiment 7 Day 11: net cost borne (expenses minus grants) +A$58 per resident [-377,+451]; spending per resident rose about A$90 more in hardest-hit councils but within normal swings; no detectable effect above these bounds. Council cash reserves per 10pp: no effect above 1.3 months (cash dip seen in fire year and year after in the >=20% burned group, suggestive only). Operating-only version (capital grants removed) could NOT be estimated because capital grants exist only from 2019-20. Rates and fee income lost specifically (own-source revenue) and rate relief reimbursement NOT tested.
best_data: OLG Time-Series Data (Your Council): rates, user charges, grants, expenses, operating result, cash (LGA (council), annual, open); Council audited financial statements (in annual reports on council websites) and Audit Office local government audit reports (LGA, annual, with some notes on rate relief and bushfire items, open); IPART rate peg decisions and special variation lists (annual reports on IPART local government functions) (LGA, annual, open)
record_ids: lit-24 lit-25 lit-51 news-43 survey-64 gov-29

name: Tourism and supply-chain spillover to unburned places
pillar_note: IL: indirect loss in neighbouring/unburned councils (spillover term); warns that burned area alone understates IL
description: Lost visitor spending flows back through suppliers, and travellers avoid whole regions -> jobs and output fall in unburned towns, other sectors and other states; some unaffected regions gain displaced spending
affected_group: Supplier industries, accommodation in non-burnt towns
key_quant_evidence: A$2.8b total output loss vs A$1.7b direct (61% spillover), ~7,300 jobs nationally, 3,171 NSW (Reiner et al. 2024, input-output model); non-affected Vic towns 10-60% cancellations (FHTA); up to 28% of Maui loss outside Maui (UHERO)
exp7_result: Spillover to unburned places was not tested. Experiment 7 compared burned vs unburned areas, so any loss in the unburned comparison group would have biased the comparison toward zero.
best_data: Tourism Region profiles (visitor spend, nights) (Tourism region (~12 in NSW), quarterly, open); Counts of Australian Businesses incl. Entries and Exits (for neighbours of burned SA2s) (SA2 (cubes used in Exp 7), industry, annual (June), open); Spendmapp card-spending data (LGA, daily/monthly, paid)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: The 61% spillover and 7,300 jobs come from an input-output model (Reiner et al.), not observed data, and input-output models tend to overstate flow-on effects. gov-4 (Deloitte) notes that spending partly moves to other regions, so local and national net losses differ. 'Strong' should be 'moderate (modelled)'.
record_ids: lit-2 survey-23 survey-22 gov-4 gov-41 lit-42

name: Financial hardship, debt stress and poverty
pillar_note: SL: financial hardship / poverty share; could use mortgage arrears or hardship-payment counts
description: Lost income plus uninsured costs -> trouble paying mortgage, rent and bills, delinquency and bankruptcy for credit-constrained households; insured owners may instead pay down debt
key_quant_evidence: Harvey: ~20% rise in bankruptcies, 13% rise in severe delinquency for uninsured credit-constrained owners (Billings et al.); Maui poverty 14% to 29% (UHERO); A$3.5m extra financial counselling (DSS)
exp7_result: Income-support (DSS) recipients: SA2 +0.21 per 1,000 per 10pp [-0.04,+0.45], not detected (rules out > about 4.5 per 1,000 at full exposure; pre-trend problem); council income support: < +0.7 per 1,000 per 10pp not detected. Council cash reserves: < 1.3 months per 10pp not detected at all-fire level (larger drawdown after most severe fires). Mortgage arrears, bankruptcy, rental hardship not tested.
best_data: DSS Benefit and Payment Recipient Demographics (incl. Commonwealth Rent Assistance, JobSeeker, Youth Allowance) (postcode, LGA, SA2 (SA2 from 2015), quarterly, open); Quarterly personal insolvency statistics (AFSA) (state; SA3 and GCCSA only from June quarter 2023, quarterly, open); Specialist Homelessness Services Collection - total clients (SA2) (SA2 (also LGA), annual, free registration)

name: Financial loss itself causes distress (incl. people outside burnt areas)
pillar_note: SL: links IL to SL; distress among indirectly affected people outside fire postcodes
description: Lost income and later money troubles -> distress and worse mental health, even for people far from the fire front; second-wave stressors predict poor recovery
key_quant_evidence: Almost three-quarters of indirectly affected respondents had anxiety symptoms up to two years on (ANU); over half of Black Saturday survivors had extra stressful events such as financial difficulty (Beyond Bushfires)
exp7_result: Not tested. Only income-support recipients (not detected) touch the financial side; no distress or mental health outcome used.
best_data: DSS payment demographics (income-support recipients) (postcode, LGA, SA2, quarterly, open); AIHW Medicare mental health services by SA3 (SA3, PHN, annual, open); HILDA Survey (restricted release can include SA4) (state; SA4 at best, annual, request/restricted)

name: Grant eligibility gaps exclude indirectly hit businesses and households
pillar_note: Moderator on IL/SL (grant access); FP: share of loss eligible for support
description: Grants require physical damage, steady income or prior profit, with sharp income thresholds -> smoke- or trade-hit firms and drought-hit farms get loans or nothing, adding debt rather than cash
key_quant_evidence: Only 7 of 90 Merimbula respondents had physical damage, so most were ineligible (Region); ~60% of SMEs wanted cash grants (NAB); 49% of support-line callers sought grant/loan help (ASBFEO)
exp7_result: Not tested directly. Indirectly, SA2 business counts were not detected to fall (Day 7), so there is no visible business loss to explain with eligibility gaps.
best_data: Performance audit report: Bushfire recovery grants (program totals and eligibility findings) (program level (PDF), program, open); NSW Special Disaster Grant recipients by LGA (rural, recent events) (LGA (aggregated where 5 or fewer recipients), per event, open); Disaster declarations and assistance measures by LGA (LGA, per declaration, open)

name: Farm capital destroyed (livestock, fencing, pasture, orchards, equipment)
pillar_note: DL: livestock deaths, fencing km and farm assets lost per council (strengthens the farm part of DL)
description: Fire kills stock and burns fences, pasture, trees and machinery -> farm capital and land value fall; farmers must buy fodder and rebuild before earning again, and drought makes it worse
key_quant_evidence: Over 56,000 livestock killed or euthanised, median 20% of stock on affected farms (Cowled et al. AVJ); A$4-5bn farm losses, 6-8% of ag output (WWF/USyd); 6,284 head lost in NSW, 5,198 in South-East NSW (NSW DPI via Farmer Magazine)
exp7_result: Only a proxy: SA2 agriculture-sector business counts (Day 10 C) not detected, +0.1% per 10 pp homes inside fire [-1.7, +1.8]; CABEE business counts not detected (fall < ~13%). Livestock, fencing and farm assets lost were not measured.
best_data: Value of Agricultural Commodities Produced 2020-21 (livestock numbers at 30 June 2021, area, businesses, gross value) by SA2 and LGA (SA2 and LGA (ASGS Ed 3), NRM, annual (Census year), open); Agricultural Commodities Australia 2019-20 (livestock at 30 June 2020, right after the fires) (SA4 and NRM only (no SA2 on this page), annual, open); Australian Agricultural Census 2020-21 dashboards (SA2 and LGA) (SA2 and LGA, annual (census), open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: The livestock counts conflict: over 56,000 (lit-30, Cowled, south-eastern Australia), over 100,000 (gov-58/survey-27, WWF modelling) and 6,284 in NSW (survey-29, early DPI count). The A$4-5bn figure is a modelled WWF/USyd estimate. Report the range and the geography of each number.

name: Local employment and earnings fall, concentrated in land- and visitor-based sectors
pillar_note: IL: jobs and wage income at workplaces inside or near the fire outline, by industry
description: Workplace damage and lost demand -> employment and wage income fall in fire areas, hardest in agriculture, retail and tourism, for up to a few years
key_quant_evidence: Black Saturday: ~10% income loss vs matched areas; agriculture -31%, retail -13%, tourism -12% (Ulubasoglu & Beaini, AJEM); Maui unemployment 2.3% to 14.2% (UHERO)
exp7_result: SA2 TOTAL income -1.6% per 10pp homes-inside-fire at year 2 [-2.7,-0.4], DETECTED, mostly fewer earners (earners -1.2% [-2.6,+0.2], income per earner -0.3% [-1.7,+1.0]). SA2 unemployment not detected (< +0.35 pts at full exposure). Sector splits (agri +0.1%, retail -2.3%, accom +6.0%, construction -1.0%) all not detected. Council income and SALM unemployment not detected. Not tested: workplace-based jobs by industry, and who the lost earners were.
best_data: Jobs in Australia (employee jobs and wages, place of work, by industry) (SA2 by industry, annual, open); Census DataPacks and TableBuilder (Place of Work, destination zone working population) (destination zone, SA1/SA2 residence, census 5-yearly, open); Small Area Labour Markets (SALM) (SA2 and LGA, quarterly, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: Spot-checked AIDR (lit-6). The sector numbers (agriculture -31%, retail -13%, tourism -12%, health +8%) are confirmed. The page summary gave employed people -8%, while the ~10% headline comes from the Deakin media release. All of these are Victoria 2009, Census 2006-2011. The Maui figures are US. Say 'not NSW' in the evidence column.

name: Delayed learning and child wellbeing harm
pillar_note: SL: NAPLAN gain in high-impact schools; child wellbeing
description: Trauma, family stress, temporary housing and smoke -> children's behaviour and test-score gains fall, with the lag showing years later
key_quant_evidence: 24,642 students: reading and numeracy gains reduced at 2 and 4 years in high-impact schools (Gibbs et al.); smoke effect on test scores nearly doubles with heavy smoke days (Stanford, ~11,700 US districts)
exp7_result: Not tested.
best_data: ACARA My School NAPLAN results by school (extract via Data Access Program) (school, annual (NAPLAN each year; 2020 not held), request/restricted); NSW government school enrolments by head count (school, annual, open)

name: Pre-existing disadvantage amplifies loss
pillar_note: Moderator on SL/IL: pre-fire SEIFA, renter share, Indigenous share as interaction terms with exposure
description: Low earners, women, renters and Aboriginal people have smaller buffers -> lose more income and wellbeing, so fires widen inequality; fire-exposed places are often already older and poorer
affected_group: Low-income people, women, renters, Aboriginal people
key_quant_evidence: Black Saturday: low-income -18%, women -14% vs men -9%, renters -14% (Ulubasoglu & Beaini); agricultural workers lost ~A$8,000/yr for two years (Ulubasoglu 2020)
exp7_result: Disadvantage tested as a predictor of housing loss: poorer councils lose more homes at the same fire size (rate ratio 1.87 [1.10, 3.14] per SD, in-sample only; no out-of-sample gain). The Experiment 6 claim that disadvantage raises socioeconomic Y vanished with the placebo-passing counterfactual (+0.09 [-0.14, +0.30]). Not tested: disadvantage as a moderator of income or earner loss at SA2.
best_data: SEIFA 2021 (IRSD, IRSAD, IER, IEO) at SA1, SA2, postcode, LGA (SA1, SA2, POA, SAL, LGA, census 5-yearly (2016 and 2021 versions), open); Census 2021 DataPacks: General Community Profile (tenure G37, income, age) and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Profile (SA1, SA2, POA, LGA, census 5-yearly, open); ATO Taxation Statistics by postcode (median/average taxable income) (postcode, annual, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: Confirmed in lit-7 (low-income -18%, women -14% vs men -9%, renters -14%). However, Experiment 7 found that the Experiment 6 claim that disadvantage raises Y vanished under the placebo check. The table should say Australian support for amplification is from Black Saturday individual data, and that Experiment 7's area-level data did not reproduce it.
record_ids: lit-7 survey-35 lit-11 survey-38 gov-25 lit-33

name: Volunteer firefighting and recovery work costs lost income
pillar_note: SL/IL: volunteer days away from paid work per council; FP: compensation payments
description: Volunteers spend weeks away from paid work or their own business -> lost income for them and their employers; compensation exists but uptake is low; volunteer recovery (fencing) shifts cost from budgets to charity time
affected_group: Volunteer firefighters, small employers, farmers helped
key_quant_evidence: 1.84 million volunteer days, A$143.5m paid leave, A$116.5m unpaid leave (Curtin final report); ~64,500 of 82,480 responders were volunteers (WSU); only 8 ACT volunteers applied for compensation
exp7_result: Not tested.
best_data: NSW RFS annual reports (volunteer numbers) (state/district, annual, open); Census DataPacks: voluntary work for an organisation (SA2) (SA1/SA2, Census 5-yearly, open)
critic_note: Critic: volunteer days away from paid work are lost labour/earnings (IL); compensation payments sit in FP.

name: Homes and buildings destroyed (direct loss base, partly insured)
pillar_note: DL: homes/facilities destroyed per council; insured claims value as a cross-check
description: Fire destroys homes, facilities and outbuildings -> direct physical loss; insurers pay part of it, so insured claims are only a fraction of the true loss and the rest falls on households and governments
key_quant_evidence: NSW: 2,448 homes and 284 facilities destroyed, A$1.88bn insurance cost (AIDR); later ICA totals 38,181 claims, A$2.32bn (Reinsurance News); insured losses about A$2.2bn (MJA-Lancet)
exp7_result: Homes destroyed per 1,000 dwellings tracks fire size (rank +0.65, Day 1). Pre-fire map predicts which councils lose homes (AUC 0.91 for Black Summer); how many homes per fire only partly predictable (Day 2). Council scale only; SA2 homes-inside-fire dose built in Day 9. Insured claims value was only quoted from the literature, not tested.
best_data: NSW RFS Building Impact Assessment reports and property-loss releases (homes/facilities destroyed by fire, dated) (fire / locality in PDF tables (no public point file found), daily to weekly (assessment dates), open); Fire Extent and Severity Mapping (FESM) 2019-20 (burn extent and severity raster) (10 m raster (cut to SA1/SA2/mesh block), fire start July 2019 to June 2020, open); NEXIS Residential Building Exposure by SA1 (building counts, 2020 version) (SA1 (2016 boundaries), snapshot (versions 2015, 2017, 2020), open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: It mixes NSW and national figures. A$1.88bn is the NSW insurance cost (AIDR), while 38,181 claims and A$2.32bn are national ICA totals. State which is which.

name: Turnover loss in undamaged businesses -> fewer hours for casual staff
pillar_note: IL: business turnover / hours worked in fire councils, including businesses with no physical damage
description: Fewer customers, travel disruption and supplier problems -> undamaged shops and food producers lose cash flow -> owners cut casual hours and let staff go
affected_group: Small business owners, casual retail and hospitality workers
key_quant_evidence: Retail -0.3% in Jan 2020, department stores -2.2%, ACT -2.3% (ABS); two-thirds of 500 SMEs affected, mostly indirectly (NAB survey)
exp7_result: SA2 retail-sector income per 10pp homes-inside-fire, years 0-2: -2.3% [-6.7,+2.1], not detected (Day 10). Business counts per SA2: fall < ~13% over two years, not detected (Day 7). Monthly turnover and hours worked were NOT tested.
best_data: Retail Trade, Australia / Monthly Household Spending Indicator (state (some industry detail), monthly, open); Spendmapp card-spending data (LGA; some postcode, daily/monthly, paid); Personal Income in Australia, wages by SA2 (SA2, annual, open)

name: Household income falls in severely burned communities
pillar_note: SL: median household/personal income change (Census 2016-2021 at SA1/SA2) by burn severity
description: Disrupted local business and tourism cut hours and jobs -> weekly personal income falls and more households have zero or negative income, most in highest-severity areas
key_quant_evidence: +1.3 percentage points of households with no or negative income vs unburnt (Akter & Grafton, The Conversation); nearly 20% of Lahaina respondents had income fall by more than half (UHERO via Civil Beat)
exp7_result: SA2 median income (ABS PIA): -0.2% per 10pp [-0.7,+0.2], not detected. SA2 total income -1.6% per 10pp at year 2 [-2.7,-0.4], DETECTED (mostly fewer earners). Council income: income fall <1.6% per 10pp residents affected (not detected). Share of households with zero/negative income not tested.
best_data: Census DataPacks GCP: household and personal weekly income, SA1 (SA1 (also SA2, POA, SAL), Census 5-yearly, open); Taxation statistics Individuals Table 8 (median and average taxable income by postcode) (postcode, annual, open); Personal Income in Australia (SA2) - used in Experiment 7 (SA2, annual, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: Checked The Conversation (news-33). The +1.3 pp rise in nil/negative-income households applies to economically disadvantaged peri-urban areas with severe burn, not to severely burned communities in general. The study is a Census 2016-2021 comparison and the article mentions no COVID control. The table should state that subgroup and the COVID caveat.

name: Responder trauma
pillar_note: SL: health of responders; X: volunteer brigade density
description: Long deployments and life-threat exposure -> PTSD and distress among firefighters and emergency staff, affecting later work and volunteering
affected_group: Fire and emergency volunteers and employees
key_quant_evidence: 4,000+ personnel; 31% of volunteers felt life at risk; probable PTSD/distress 4.2% volunteers, 7.3% employees two years on (Curtin After the Fires)
exp7_result: Not tested.
best_data: NSW RFS annual reports (membership, brigades, districts) (state, some district tables, annual, open)

name: Multi-year lag in farm income (replanting, herd rebuild, delayed claims)
pillar_note: IL: farm income / agricultural output in fire-hit councils, 1-5 years after
description: Burnt orchards, herds and crops take years to come back, and slow insurance claims mean missed planting seasons -> farm income stays low for several years; families take off-farm jobs to fill the gap
key_quant_evidence: About 2 years before farm income resumes; 13,300 of 14,000 plants lost, 4-5 years to recover production (ABC Rural)
exp7_result: Only the worker-side was tested: SA2 agriculture-sector income change per 10pp homes-inside-fire, years 0-2, +0.1% [-1.7,+1.8], not detected (Day 10). Farm output, herd and orchard recovery, and years 3-5 were NOT tested. SA2 total income -1.6% per 10pp at year 2 was detected but is not split by farm vs non-farm.
best_data: Value of Agricultural Commodities Produced (regional cubes) (SA2 (regional data cubes; state/national headline), annual (financial year), open); Agricultural Commodities, Australia (census-year area/head counts) (SA2 (census years); state otherwise, annual survey, full census every 5 years, open); ABARES farm survey results (AGSURF / farm data portal) (ABARES region (large groupings), not SA2, annual, open)

name: Forestry supply shock -> mill jobs lost
pillar_note: IL: jobs in wood/timber manufacturing workplaces in forestry councils (Snowy Valleys, Bega Valley)
description: Plantations and native forest burn -> burnt logs sell for a fraction of value and sawlog supply drops for decades -> mills close or cut staff; a few salvage mills hire temporarily
affected_group: Timber workers, mills, Snowy Valleys economy
key_quant_evidence: 50,000 of 168,000 ha of regional softwood plantation burnt; 42% salvaged; softwood employs 11,000+ in the region (ABC Rural 2023); about 5,000 jobs depend on the A$2bn Riverina industry (ABC 2020)
exp7_result: Forestry/wood-manufacturing jobs were not one of the sectors tested in Experiment 7 (sectors were agriculture, retail, accommodation and food, construction). Total SA2 income detected a fall of -1.6% per 10pp at year 2, which could partly include mill workers but is not split.
best_data: Jobs in Australia (employee jobs and wages by industry and place of work) (SA2 by ANZSIC industry (some SA2-industry cells suppressed), annual (financial year), open); Census DataPacks: Place of Work (destination zone) by industry (Destination zone / POW, census 5-yearly, open); NSW Fire Extent and Severity Mapping (FESM) (10 m raster / polygons, per fire season, open)

name: Smoke -> missed work and lower productivity far from fires
pillar_note: IL: smoke-day exposure as an IL driver separate from burned area
description: Smoke makes workers sick or stay home -> hours and earnings fall even in cities with no fire, a productivity loss
key_quant_evidence: Each extra smoke day lowers quarterly earnings ~0.1% (Borgschulte et al., US); 1.8 million Australians missed work, A$1.3bn+ output (Australia Institute poll); Sydney smoke A$12-50m/day (Climate Council)
exp7_result: Smoke exposure and sick days were not tested; Experiment 7 used burned area only, so smoke hitting people far from the fire is outside what it measured.
best_data: NSW air quality hourly PM2.5 by station (station (~50-90), hourly, open); Personal Income in Australia and Jobs in Australia (earnings by SA2) (SA2, annual, open); Medicare Benefits Schedule and PBS statistics by SA3 (SA3 (MBS), monthly, open)
critic_note: Evidence caveat: The 1.8 million missed-work figure is from an Australia Institute online poll (an advocacy organisation, extrapolated to the population). The per-smoke-day earnings effect is from US data. Flag it as indicative only.

name: Evacuation keeps workers away from jobs
pillar_note: IL: work days lost to evacuation (evacuation orders x population) as a short-run IL term
description: Evacuation and road closures keep people from work; the longer they are away, the more work and income are lost, and some do not return to work for months
key_quant_evidence: 55% of those away more than a night said it reduced their ability to work vs 37% (IDMC); about 1 in 4 Fort McMurray evacuated workers not back in paid work at follow-up (CMAJ Open)
exp7_result: Evacuation days and work days lost were not tested in Experiment 7.
best_data: Emergency warnings / evacuation orders (RFS, SES, Emergency Alert archive) (warning polygon / LGA, hourly, request/restricted); Mesh Block / SA1 population and workers (Census) (Mesh Block / SA1, census 5-yearly, open); NSW Fire Extent and Severity Mapping / NSW RFS fire polygons (polygons, final extent; daily progression for major fires on request, open)

name: Moving away after the fire costs income
pillar_note: SL: household income of movers vs stayers; population change in fire councils
description: Households that relocate lose local networks and well-matched jobs -> larger income loss than those who stay; overseas evidence says the effect may fade within a few years
key_quant_evidence: Relocators about -19% income (Ulubasoglu & Beaini); Katrina displaced: small, mostly temporary income effects (Deryugina et al.)
exp7_result: Experiment 7 tested the area outcome, not movers vs stayers. SA2 population: -0.4% per 10pp of homes inside fire [-2.2,+1.4], not detected (drifts to -0.6% by years 3-5). SA2 total income -1.6% per 10pp at year 2 [-2.7,-0.4], DETECTED, mostly fewer earners (leaving vs not earning is unresolved). Median income not detected (-0.2% [-0.7,+0.2]).
best_data: Census DataPacks: usual address 1 year / 5 years ago (UAI1P, UAI5P, PUR5P coded to SA2) (SA1/SA2/POA (origin coded to SA2), Census 5-yearly, open); Regional Internal Migration Estimates (SA2) 2006-07 to 2015-16 and Net Internal and Overseas Migration by Age (SA2) 2017-2020 (SA2, annual (financial year), open); Regional population by SA2 (ERP) 2001-25 (already used in Experiment 7 Day 10) (SA2, annual, open)
critic_note: Critic: movers vs stayers needs linked individual data (restricted); area data cannot test it.

name: Lower life satisfaction (wellbeing cost)
pillar_note: SL: wellbeing score (HILDA life satisfaction) as an SL indicator
description: Disaster -> life satisfaction lower for 18+ months; valued in dollars this is a large cost not in damage tallies
key_quant_evidence: Significantly lower life satisfaction after 18 months (HILDA, Life Course Centre); willingness to pay ~A$2,991 per household per year for 1% less impact (Ambrey et al.)
exp7_result: Not tested; no wellbeing measure used.
best_data: HILDA Survey (life satisfaction) (state; SA4 only in restricted release, annual waves, request/restricted)

name: Unpaid recovery work falls on women
pillar_note: SL: Census unpaid domestic work hours by sex
description: Clean-up, caring and household recovery work increase -> more unpaid hours, mostly women, less time for paid work
key_quant_evidence: +1.7 pp women vs +1.0 pp men doing 15+ unpaid hours/week in burnt areas (Akter & Grafton)
exp7_result: Not tested.
best_data: Census GCP: unpaid domestic work hours by age by sex (SA1 and SA2) (SA1, SA2, Census 5-yearly, open)

name: School closures and displacement disrupt schooling
pillar_note: SL: school closure days / attendance in fire councils
description: Fires close schools, damage facilities, take teachers away and displace children -> lost school days and more counselling and food support needs
key_quant_evidence: About 600 NSW schools closed in late 2019 (CESE media summary); about 64,600 new displacements recorded (IDMC)
exp7_result: Not tested.
best_data: NSW government school enrolments by head count (by school) (school (with location), annual, open); Attendance rate at government schools, NSW (state only, annual, open); ACARA My School and Data Access Program (school-level attendance, NAPLAN, enrolment) (school, annual, request/restricted)

name: Social ties protect recovery
pillar_note: Moderator on SL: volunteering / community group rates as a protective X variable
description: Strong community and group membership -> better recovery and resilience (though close ties also mean more personal loss)
key_quant_evidence: Almost 80% reported some resilience; about two-thirds return to pre-disaster wellbeing (ANU survey)
exp7_result: Not tested. No community-tie or volunteering variable has been used.
best_data: Census 2021 G23 Voluntary work for an organisation or group by age by sex (SA2 (also LGA; SA1 in DataPacks), census 5-yearly, open); Census DataPacks (General Community Profile) for same-address-5-years-ago (stability) and household composition (SA1, SA2, census 5-yearly, open)

name: Hidden fiscal cost through ordinary transfers and flow-on costs
pillar_note: FP: welfare/JobSeeker recipients per LGA after fire as a hidden-cost indicator
description: Beyond visible disaster aid, governments pay more in unemployment, health and welfare transfers for years plus clean-up and temporary housing -> true fiscal cost is a multiple of reported aid
key_quant_evidence: US hurricanes: fiscal cost per person ~US$150 rises to at least US$780 with transfers (Deryugina); Australia disasters A$38bn/yr average (Deloitte)
exp7_result: Experiment 7: SA2 DSS welfare not detected (rise < +4.5 per 1,000); council DSS income support not detected (< +0.7 per 1,000); SALM unemployment (council) not detected; SA2 unemployment not detected (< +0.35 pts at full exposure). Health, clean-up and temporary housing costs not tested.
best_data: DSS Payment Demographic Data (quarterly) (SA2, postcode, LGA, electorate, quarterly, open); Location-Based Disaster Assistance Payments (LGA, per event, open); ABS/JSA Small Area Labour Markets (SALM) (SA2 and LGA, quarterly, open)

name: Property values and the rate base
pillar_note: FP: rateable land values (NSW Valuer General) in fire councils; SL: household wealth
description: Buyers re-price fire risk (values dip near fire zones) but housing shortage can push rebuilt-town prices up -> changes household wealth and the council rate base
key_quant_evidence: California 2018-21: homes farther from past fires ~2% higher value (FRBSF); Kinglake prices ~+150% in 10 years (analyst comment)
exp7_result: Experiment 7 Day 10 rents (NSW Fair Trading new bonds, council level, year after): +0.1% per 10 homes per 1,000 [-1.6,+1.2], not detected. Property sale prices, land values and the council rate base were NOT tested.
best_data: NSW Valuer General Bulk Property Sales Information (PSI) (individual property with address, postcode and LGA, weekly updates; each sale has a contract and settlement date, open); NSW Valuer General Bulk Land Value information (individual property (one CSV per LGA), annual valuing date (1 July) with monthly file refresh; up to 5 valuing years per file, open); ABS Total Value of Dwellings (mean price and number of dwellings) (state and capital city / rest-of-state in the download; methodology uses SA2 but SA2 tables are not shown in the release page I fetched, quarterly, open)
critic_note: Critic: NSW rates are pegged (IPART), so value changes shift rates between ratepayers rather than cut council revenue; household wealth (SL), weak FP link. Evidence caveat: 'Kinglake +150% in 10 years' is an agent or analyst comment with no comparison area. The only systematic evidence is from California (FRBSF).

name: Housing loss drives workers out -> local labour shortage
pillar_note: IL: labour supply / job vacancies in fire towns; links SL housing to IL
description: Destroyed homes and rising rents -> teachers, nurses, shop and mill staff leave -> employers cannot fill jobs and local services thin even as demand returns
affected_group: Essential and service workers, local employers
key_quant_evidence: Mallacoota: only 15 of 120 destroyed homes rebuilt, modest 3BR rent A$170 to A$370/week (ABC)
exp7_result: SA2 rents and SA2 population: not detected (Exp 7). Job vacancies and unfilled posts were NOT tested. Mallacoota-style housing loss in a few small towns may be too small to move SA2 averages.
best_data: Internet Vacancy Index (regional, by occupation) (ABS regions (large, e.g. NSW South Coast), state, monthly, open); Rental bond lodgements, refunds and holdings (postcode, monthly (lodgements), quarterly (refunds), annual (holdings), open); ABS Regional Population by SA2 (SA2, annual (June), open)

name: Smoke taint on grapes and wine
pillar_note: IL: farm income in wine regions; smoke days as the exposure (not burned area)
description: Smoke taints grapes -> crops rejected or wine unsaleable, plus fewer cellar-door visitors -> winery income falls even without flames
key_quant_evidence: Industry estimate about A$40m, NSW association up to A$100m incl. tourism (ABC/MDPI)
exp7_result: Smoke exposure and wine-region income were not tested. Experiment 7 used burned area / homes-inside-fire only, so a smoke-only loss in unburned vineyards was invisible to it.
best_data: National Vintage Report (crush by Geographical Indication region) (GI region (e.g. Hunter Valley, Canberra District, Tumbarumba, Shoalhaven Coast), annual vintage, open); NSW air quality hourly PM2.5 / visibility (~50-90 monitoring stations, hourly, open); Copernicus CAMS atmospheric reanalysis (PM2.5 grid) (~40 km grid, 3-hourly, free registration)

name: Cost shifting between governments and onto private owners
pillar_note: FP: unfunded share of council recovery costs (DRFA claims vs council spend)
description: Reimbursement rules shift costs up to the Commonwealth (weak mitigation incentive) and down to councils/ratepayers for unfunded items; Crown land exemption shifts fence costs to farmers
affected_group: Councils, farmers next to state forest, taxpayers
key_quant_evidence: Commonwealth paid up to 75% of state recovery costs above thresholds (Productivity Commission)
exp7_result: Experiment 7 Day 11 net cost (expenses minus grants) +A$58 per resident [-377,+451], i.e. no detectable shift to councils above these bounds, consistent with reimbursement covering most. Unfunded share, private fence costs and Crown-land exemptions not tested.
best_data: DRFA Activation History by LGA (LGA, per event, open); OLG Time-Series Data (grants vs expenses) (LGA, annual, open); NSW Treasury / Commonwealth DRFA payment tables (Budget Paper No. 3) (State, annual, open)

name: Tourism dependence and peak-season timing set exposure
pillar_note: X: tourism/ag/forestry employment share and fire month as exposure variables in the RF
description: Councils with big tourism, agriculture or forestry shares, hit during the Christmas peak, lose much more for the same fire
key_quant_evidence: 202 interviews and 1,004 survey responses on Christmas-period displacement (BNHCRC Hazard Note 95)
exp7_result: Sector business counts tested at SA2 (Day 10 C): accommodation and food +6.0% [-0.4, +12.4], retail -2.3% [-6.7, +2.1], not detected. The interaction of tourism dependence with fire month (Christmas peak) was not tested.
best_data: Census 2021 DataPacks: industry of employment (accommodation and food, agriculture, forestry) by place of usual residence (SA1, SA2, LGA, census 5-yearly, open); Census Place of Work (POWP) and Working Population by destination zone (destination zone (finest), SA2, LGA, census 5-yearly, free registration); Tourism Research Australia LGA visitor and accommodation profiles (visitors, nights, spend) (92 regional NSW LGAs, annual (survey, with sample noise), open)

name: Compounding disasters slow recovery
pillar_note: Moderator / X: number of declared disasters in prior and following years per LGA
description: Fires followed by COVID, floods and mice -> relief centres close, bookings stay weak and capacity to recover erodes
key_quant_evidence: Eurobodalla agency occupancy ~50% weekday, ~70% weekend to mid-December 2022 (About Regional)
exp7_result: Day 9 listed COVID (2020-21) and the 2022 floods as caveats in the post-fire years, but no test of compounding disasters as a moderator was run.
best_data: DRFA Activation History by LGA (LGA, per event (dates), open); NSW declared natural disasters list (LGA, per event, open); NSW Rental Bond Lodgement (monthly by postcode) (postcode, monthly, open)
critic_note: Critic: count of declared disasters before/after each fire per LGA is a covariate/moderator X, not a Y part.

name: Deaths and injuries
pillar_note: DL: deaths and injuries per 100,000 (severity tiers)
description: Fire kills and injures people (lost lives, burns, long recovery).
critic_note: added by critic

name: Public infrastructure and council assets damaged
pillar_note: DL: infrastructure damage; cost side in FP (DRFA restoration claims)
description: Roads, bridges, water/sewer, halls destroyed; the repair bill then flows to FP.
critic_note: added by critic

name: Destroyed homes owned by non-residents (holiday homes)
pillar_note: X / moderator of DL -> IL/SL: pre-fire unoccupied-dwelling share (Census 2016)
description: Where many lost homes were holiday homes, the loss falls on owners living elsewhere, so local resident income and jobs move less.
best_data: ABS Census 2016 GCP DataPack: unoccupied private dwellings by SA1/SA2 (open)
critic_note: added by critic

name: Insurance payouts as a local money inflow
pillar_note: Moderator of DL -> SL/IL (insured share of loss)
description: Claims paid replace lost wealth and pay local builders, cushioning local income.
critic_note: added by critic

name: Concurrent drought amplifies and confounds farm loss
pillar_note: X: pre-fire rainfall deciles / drought status per council
description: The 2017-20 drought made farm fire losses worse and blurs any fire-only farm effect.
critic_note: added by critic

name: Government-funded clean-up and debris removal
pillar_note: FP: clean-up spending per destroyed home
description: State and Commonwealth paid to clear destroyed properties (a large cost per destroyed home).
critic_note: added by critic

name: Park, forest and road closures extend tourism loss
pillar_note: IL: park-closure days per council (tourism loss duration)
description: National parks and state forests stayed closed for months, so visitor loss outlasts the fire.
critic_note: added by critic

name: Aboriginal cultural and Country loss
pillar_note: SL: note only (hard to measure)
description: Loss of cultural sites and Country is a separate social loss for Aboriginal communities (Royal Commission).
critic_note: added by critic

name: Bank hardship deferrals hide financial stress
pillar_note: Moderator of SL hardship timing
description: Mortgage deferrals after the fires (then COVID) delay arrears for 6-12 months.
critic_note: added by critic

name: Capital recovery spending and disaster grants / DRFA reimbursement
pillar_note: FP: council capital purchases (cash-flow statement) and natural-disaster grant lines in audited financial statements and Quarterly Budget Review Statements; being collected in Experiment 10 (not duplicated here)
description: Councils spend on rebuilding roads, bridges and buildings; part is reimbursed later through disaster grants (DRFA), with timing gaps and unfunded parts.
best_data: NSW council audited financial statements + Quarterly Budget Review Statements (being collected in Experiment 10)
critic_note: added by Ray (2 Oct)
